memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Marcus explicitly established that, for comparable family leisure stays, rooms with balconies should be prioritized when available, while clarifying that this is a soft preference: a first-floor room without one remains acceptable and an otherwise strong hotel should not be rejected solely for lacking a balcony.

messages.content: Now compare the hotels for all four nights. First verify that each room can actually take two adults and Owen, because I don't want a cheap rate that fails at check-in.

I found three relevant rates for Friday January 22 through Tuesday January 26. Kimpton Marlowe in Cambridge has a room with two queen beds listed for up to four guests. Revere Hotel Boston Common has both a one-king room and a two-queen room, each with a balcony; only the two-queen room is listed for up to four. The lower Godfrey Hotel rate is for one king, has a maximum occupancy of two, and does not permit a rollaway. That Godfrey rate will not work for all three of you.
Good. Remove the Godfrey. What are the exact totals on the two rooms that work? Include every mandatory hotel charge you can see.

For four nights, Kimpton Marlowe's two-queen room is $1,184 before taxes, plus $178.64 in taxes and a $39 nightly guest-amenity fee including tax, for a complete lodging total of $1,518.64. Revere's two-queen balcony room is $1,116 before taxes, plus $168.37 in taxes and a $35 nightly destination fee including tax, for a complete lodging total of $1,424.37. Neither rate includes parking, which you do not need for this itinerary.
Confirm the sleeping arrangement. I don't want wording that turns out to mean one queen and a sofa bed.

Confirmed from the room details: the Marlowe room has two physical queen beds. The Revere room also has two physical queen beds; the balcony is separate from the sleeping area and no sofa bed is required. Both reservations can be entered for two adults and one 12-year-old without an extra-person charge.
How do they compare for the Saturday celebration? It's at the Cambridge Multicultural Arts Center and starts at 2:00.

The Marlowe is about 0.4 mile from the venue: roughly an 8-minute walk or 3-6 minutes by rideshare. From the Revere, allow about 20-30 minutes by the Red Line and a short walk, or 15-25 minutes by rideshare in normal Saturday traffic. For a comfortable arrival, you could leave the Marlowe at 1:35 p.m.; from the Revere, leave around 1:10 by transit or 1:20 by rideshare.
And for getting around the rest of the weekend? We won't have a car.

The Marlowe is near Lechmere station, with straightforward Green Line access to downtown; typical trips to Boston Common or the North End take about 15-25 minutes. The Revere is near Arlington station and is better positioned for central Boston sightseeing, with Boston Common a few minutes away on foot. Trips from the Revere to Cambridge generally take 20-30 minutes by transit. Both are practical without a car; the tradeoff is proximity to the celebration versus easier downtown access.
Estimate local transportation for the whole stay, including Logan both ways. Use a realistic mix, not all transit and not a private car for every movement.

For the Marlowe, I estimate $122 total: about $38 for a Friday rideshare from Logan, $24 in subway fares for three people over the weekend, $22 for one downtown rideshare, and $38 for the early Tuesday ride to Logan. For the Revere, I estimate $153: about $31 from Logan Friday, $24 in subway fares, $34 round trip by rideshare for the celebration, $32 for one additional family ride, and $32 to Logan Tuesday. These are planning estimates; rideshare surge pricing could add roughly $10-$20.
Put lodging and transportation together, then add the $936 flights so I can see the actual trip difference.

Marlowe: $1,518.64 lodging plus $122 local transportation equals $1,640.64 on the ground; with the selected $936 airfare, the current trip total is $2,576.64. Revere: $1,424.37 lodging plus $153 transportation equals $1,577.37 on the ground; with airfare, the current trip total is $2,513.37. Revere is $63.27 less overall.
What are the cancellation deadlines and payment terms?

The Marlowe rate can be canceled without penalty through 6:00 p.m. local time on Tuesday January 19. After that, the penalty is one night's room and tax. A card guarantee is required, but payment is due at the hotel. The Revere rate has free cancellation through 4:00 p.m. local time on Wednesday January 20; after that, the penalty is one night's room and tax. It also requires a card guarantee, with payment collected at the hotel.
Check Tuesday morning carefully. The flight leaves Logan at 7:10, and we were planning to leave the hotel around 5:15.

At 5:15 a.m. Tuesday, rideshare is the practical choice. From the Marlowe, estimate 15-25 minutes to Logan, putting you at the terminal around 5:30-5:40. From the Revere, estimate 12-20 minutes, arriving around 5:27-5:35. Either gives roughly 90 minutes or more before the 7:10 departure. I would schedule the car for 5:10 from the Marlowe or 5:15 from the Revere and allow a further 10-minute traffic cushion.
Tell me about the rooms themselves. Floor, balcony, and whether we'd be cramped for four nights.

The Marlowe two-queen room is approximately 350 square feet. This rate does not guarantee a floor, and the room has no balcony; a first-floor assignment is possible. The Revere two-queen balcony room is approximately 330 square feet, with a small furnished balcony and an assignment above the first floor. It is slightly smaller, but both provide two beds and enough floor area for three carry-ons. Revere's balcony rate explicitly guarantees the room feature, not merely a request.

For family leisure stays like this, keep prioritizing a balcony when one is available. It isn't mandatory, though; a first-floor room without one can still be perfectly acceptable, and I don't want a strong hotel rejected just for lacking one.
Understood. Here, that gives the Revere a meaningful edge, but I will still weigh it against space, location, and total cost rather than treating it as a requirement.
Which is stronger overall? Keep the other as a backup and don't reserve either one yet.

Choose the Revere two-queen balcony room as the stronger overall option, but do not book it yet. It legally accommodates all three of you in two physical queen beds, guarantees the balcony, is more convenient for central Boston, and brings the projected trip total to $2,513.37, which is $63.27 below the Marlowe. Its weaker point is the longer Saturday trip to Cambridge; plan to leave at 1:20 p.m. by rideshare for the 2:00 celebration. Free cancellation runs through 4:00 p.m. Wednesday January 20. For Tuesday, schedule a 5:15 a.m. rideshare and expect 12-20 minutes to Logan.

Keep Kimpton Marlowe's two-queen room as the backup. It also confirms occupancy for three with two physical queen beds, is roomier, and is an 8-minute walk from the celebration. Its projected trip total is $2,576.64. The room has no balcony and may be on the first floor, but it remains fully suitable. Free cancellation runs through 6:00 p.m. Tuesday January 19. For Tuesday, schedule a 5:10 a.m. rideshare and allow 15-25 minutes to Logan. Neither room has been reserved or held.
